record.paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of infinite dimensional algebras
record.context_brief: GS algebras and finite GK images
record.original_question: Let A be a Golod-Shafarevich algebra: a graded algebra A = <X | R = 0> over a field K, where X has m degree-one generators, R is a graded relator subspace in degrees at least two with Hilbert series H_R(t), and there exists a number t_0 in (0,1) such that H_R(t) converges at t_0 and 1 - m t_0 + H_R(t_0) < 0. Must every such Golod-Shafarevich algebra have a homomorphic image that is both infinite-dimensional and of finite Gelfand-Kirillov dimension?

evidence.quote: If A has such a presentation then we say that A is a GS-algebra.
Problem 5. Is it true that an arbitrary GS-algebra has an infinite dimensional homomorphic image of finite GK-dimension?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let K be a field and let A be a graded associative K-algebra presented as A = K⟨X | R⟩, where X = {x_1, …, x_m} is a finite set of m degree-one generators (m ≥ 2) and R is a graded subspace of the free algebra K⟨X⟩ contained in the part of degree at least 2; the elements of R serve as homogeneous defining relations. Let H_R(t) = Σ_{n≥2} dim_K(R_n) t^n be the Hilbert series of R. Suppose A satisfies the Golod–Shafarevich condition: there exists t_0 ∈ (0,1) such that the series H_R(t_0) converges and

   1 − m t_0 + H_R(t_0) < 0.

The Gelfand–Kirillov (GK) dimension of a finitely generated K-algebra B with generating subspace V is GKdim(B) = lim sup_{n→∞} log_n dim_K(V^n), and it is independent of the chosen finite-dimensional generating subspace.

Question: Must every such Golod–Shafarevich algebra A admit a homomorphic image that is both infinite-dimensional over K and of finite Gelfand–Kirillov dimension?
artifact.status_search_result: The question (attributed to Zelmanov) was answered negatively by Alexander Iyudu and Agata Smoktunowicz-type results: there exist Golod–Shafarevich algebras that cannot be homomorphically mapped onto any infinite-dimensional algebra of finite Gelfand–Kirillov dimension. This was established in work on "GK-dimension of algebras with many generic relations" (Glasgow Mathematical Journal / Advances in Mathematics 222 (2009) 2107–2116), explicitly answering Zelmanov's question.

status_evidence.title: GK-dimension of algebras with many generic relations
status_evidence.snippet: there are Golod-Shafarevich algebras which cannot be homomorphically mapped onto infinite dimensional algebras with finite Gelfand-Kirillov dimension. This answers a question of Zelmanov.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is solved negatively: not every GS-algebra admits an infinite-dimensional homomorphic image of finite GK-dimension.

status_evidence.title: Advances in Mathematics 222 (2009) 2107–2116
status_evidence.snippet: Article on GK-dimension and generic relations addressing Zelmanov's question on Golod–Shafarevich algebras.
status_evidence.claim: Published resolution appears in Advances in Mathematics, 2009.
